summary: Fixed release security finding SEC-1 (MEDIUM): the anonymous webhook boundary processed form/multipart request bodies before authenticating because ASP.NET Core MVC model binding materializes the form value providers before the action runs. Added WebhookAuthenticationFilter, an IAsyncAuthorizationFilter applied to ArrTagsWebhookController with [TypeFilter]. Authorization filters run before model binding, so the filter authenticates the X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header through the existing ADR-005 versioned lease with the same bounded (1024-char) constant-time comparison and fails closed with the uniform 401 before any body read for every content type; after authenticating it rejects a non-JSON content type with a bounded 400 before the read, so OperationalLimits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes (default 256 KiB) is the effective bound and the framework form limits are never reached. The action still re-authenticates and applies the byte bound and tolerant parse, so the public ReceiveAsync entry point and the JSON contract are unchanged. No provider, state, artwork, or configuration behavior changed. Attempt 2 corrects the one documentation defect the independent reviewer returned (SEC1-DOC-1, MEDIUM): README.md lines 511-517 still stated the pre-SEC-1 test counts; they are now the post-SEC-1 totals (1,288 total / 1,228 default / 1,244 host-guarded) consistent with docs/limitations.md and docs/changelog.md, and the trailing attribution sentence now records that the counts reflect the current post-SEC-1 suite rather than the task 7.5 clean build.
mechanism: Pre-model-binding IAsyncAuthorizationFilter ([TypeFilter(typeof(WebhookAuthenticationFilter))] on the controller). Authorization filters run before ControllerActionInvoker.ActionBegin, which unconditionally calls CompositeValueProvider.CreateAsync and therefore invokes the form value providers that read and parse form bodies. Short-circuiting in the authorization filter prevents the read. Chosen over removing [ApiController] (does not stop the composite value provider) and over [Consumes] alone (a resource filter runs after authorization, so an unauthenticated non-JSON request would not return the uniform 401). The filter reads only the secret header and the current public configuration snapshot and performs no plugin work before authenticating; the action's own authentication is retained as defence in depth so the public/testable ReceiveAsync behavior is preserved.

known_limitations: The filter and the action both authenticate the request (two bounded constant-time comparisons and lease acquisitions per authenticated request). This is deliberate defence in depth that preserves the public/testable ReceiveAsync entry point; it has no behavioral effect.

An authenticated non-JSON body is rejected with 400 Bad Request rather than 415 Unsupported Media Type. The task explicitly accepted a bounded 400/413; 400 was chosen to match the existing ADR-012 payload-rejection status and avoid adding a new documented status. An unauthenticated non-JSON body still returns the uniform 401.

The route now treats a body with no declared content type as JSON (compatibility) and accepts application/json, text/json, and any +json structured suffix; a JSON body sent with an unrelated content type (for example text/plain) is rejected with 400. Sonarr and Radarr send application/json, so no real delivery is affected.

The new automated regression test is an in-process MVC-pipeline test, not a Kestrel/HTTP host test. The decisive live HTTP verification was performed manually on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host and is recorded here and in docs/changelog.md, but it is not an automated host-guarded fact in the default suite.

docs/release/build-and-release.md and docs/limitations.md now record the post-fix artifact identity; the task 7.5 clean-checkout reproducibility evidence they contain remains the pre-fix evidence and is labelled as such. The re-run release review re-verifies end-to-end publication on the new artifact.

The pre-SEC-1 counts (1,278 / 1,218 / 1,234) remain in historical records (docs/implementation/7.5/reviewer-report.json and the release-0.1.0-sec1 reviewer/orchestration reports that quote the pre-fix README text); these are historical records and were intentionally left unchanged.
